title: 13 Employees. $1 Billion. 18 Months. #shorts
description:
In April twenty twelve, Facebook bought Instagram for one billion dollars. The app was about eighteen months old and had just thirteen employees.
Follow for more fortunes made and lost.
first_comment: Did they sell too early, or was one billion the smartest exit ever? 👇

lines.text: Thirteen employees. One billion dollars. Eighteen months.
How does an app that young get that price?
Instagram started as a check-in app called Burbn. Almost nobody used it.
So the founders cut everything except photos and filters.
On launch day, twenty-five thousand people signed up.
Within eighteen months, it had over thirty million users.
Then it launched on Android, and grew even faster.
Days later, Facebook offered one billion dollars. The deal was agreed in a single weekend.
A billion dollars, for thirteen people and a photo app.
